match_note: Round-1 reports quote and cite text and figures that appear verbatim in arXiv v1: R3's line-referenced phrases ('By integrating spectral weight', 'essential mechanism', 'This smaller gap', 'To better'), Fig. 1e monolayer 1T band structure, Fig. 3a/3h, Fig. 4b/4d/4e, Supplementary Figs. 3, 9, 10, ref. [48], the TK~40 K estimate, U/W~1.67, ~12-13% of clusters, 'coherent' peak wording. R1's round-2 quotes ('the breakdown of the Kondo explanation is evident...') are v1 sentences. None of the round-1 additions (vortex maps, 25 K and 78 K data, pristine-sample data, XRD, 4Hb slab DFT, 'metallic peak' wording) are in v1. Four review rounds (Versions 0-3); R1 and R3 sign off in round 3, R2 in round 4.

concerns.quote: I would also like to see a similar quantitative comparison with the Brinkman-Rice. ... what if the quantitative match with Brinkman-Rice is even worse? If you are deciding between two scenarios, they should be treated equally.
concerns.summary: Kondo is excluded by a quantitative mismatch with the Anderson impurity model, but the favoured Brinkman-Rice picture is never tested quantitatively in the same way.

concerns.quote: I suggest trying to fit the HWHM data with T_K being a fitting parameter. (R1) / Can't this be explained more easily by the fact that the Tk estimation of 40K is wrong? (R3)
concerns.summary: The 40 K Kondo temperature estimate may simply be wrong; fit the HWHM with T_K free and test how sensitive the conclusion is to the assumed T_K (e.g. 10 K).
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Please provide a reference for the expression used to estimate T_K.
concerns.summary: The Anderson-model formula used to estimate T_K is given without a citation.

concerns.quote: Isn't it better to look at the HWHM vs T in the range of 4K - 40K? Since the material becomes SC below 3K, it may change screening conditions and affect the kondo peak
concerns.summary: The 0.3 to 4.2 K window for the peak-width temperature dependence straddles the superconducting transition, which could change screening and distort the width; measure 4 to 40 K instead.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the authors observe this peak all the way to the filling of one, which is the half filled purely Mott insulating state. Shouldn't the spectral function of a Mott insulator be just a LHB and an UHB?
concerns.summary: A central peak persisting at half filling (in data and DMFT) contradicts a Mott insulator with U/W=1.67, which should show only Hubbard bands (R3 asks the same of the DFT/U choice).
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Is it possible to develop such a coherence in a disordered system? ... this state exists on ~12% of the sites randomly distributed in real space. (R1)
concerns.summary: A coherent Brinkman-Rice quasiparticle is a lattice concept; invoking it (alongside a single-impurity Kondo picture) for randomly placed, locally doped clusters is not justified.

concerns.quote: How valid is the single-impurity model, given that 13% of the sites have this zero-bias peak? Should one consider a kondo-lattice model instead?
concerns.summary: The Kondo exclusion uses a single-impurity Anderson model although 13% of sites host the peak, so a Kondo-lattice treatment may be needed.

concerns.quote: they study samples lightly doped with Se. How does the physics they observe translate into clean samples?
concerns.summary: All data are on 0.5% Se-doped crystals; it is unclear whether the physics holds in pristine 4Hb-TaS2.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: A very similar work has been done on a very similar 1T/1H-NbSe2 heterostructure ... How do the authors here go beyond that work? Why is the interpretation of the observed peak different to this work?
concerns.summary: A closely related NbSe2 study reports a similar metal-Mott transition; the advance over it, and why the peak is interpreted differently, is unclear.

concerns.quote: Why in NbSe2 heterostructure the doping is so different - the flat band is mostly occupied, whereas here in 4Hb-TaS2 it is mostly unoccupied?
concerns.summary: The opposite flat-band filling in the NbSe2 analogue is unexplained.

concerns.quote: the top 1T layer studied here has 1H layer only on one side, unlike in the bulk ... I am not sure how much of the observed physics can be extrapolated to the bulk.
concerns.summary: The surface 1T layer has a 1H neighbour on one side only, so its charge transfer and filling may be a surface effect not representative of the bulk.

concerns.quote: Supplementary Fig. 3 shows that the local doping level is very different on a CDW site and between CDW sites. This is very surprising, how is this possible?
concerns.summary: The strong difference in local doping between cluster centres and inter-cluster regions needs a physical explanation.

concerns.quote: I would like the authors to elaborate on the idea that the paramagnetic puddles could explain the interlayer negative Josephson coupling.
concerns.summary: The link from paramagnetic puddles to negative interlayer Josephson coupling is asserted without explanation.

concerns.quote: What is the unstrained inter-layer spacing? I would appreciate if they could provide some more details ... on how precisely they control the filling
concerns.summary: The unstrained interlayer spacing, which underlies the charge-transfer argument, is not reported.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: If the Se substitution is responsible for the doping, shouldn't it have a discreet charge transfer per SoD ... Did the authors compute the DFT of the SoD with different Se substitutions (R3)
concerns.summary: How dilute Se substitution produces a continuous range of cluster fillings up to near half filling is unexplained; DFT by Se site and concentration, and an interstitial or structural-perturbation alternative, are not considered.

concerns.quote: one might suppose a more theoretically relevant model would be the periodic Anderson model ... Can the authors justify the choice of a single-band model?
concerns.summary: A single-band Hubbard DMFT ignores the dispersive 1H band, charge transfer and Kondo screening that a periodic Anderson model would capture.

concerns.quote: hole-doping a periodic Anderson model gives rise to a narrow resonance at the Fermi level flanking the lower Hubbard band ... Could the authors comment on whether this mechanism is compatible with their observations?
concerns.summary: A narrow Fermi-level resonance from interband singlet formation in a hole-doped periodic Anderson model could produce the same peak.

concerns.quote: do the NRG and QMC data agree? Why were two simulation methods employed? A dedicated section in the supplemental information describing and comparing the methods would be of great help
concerns.summary: The two DMFT solvers are not described or compared.

concerns.quote: 'By integrating spectral weight...' Can the authors please explain this computation in more detail?
concerns.summary: The method for computing electron filling per SoD cluster from integrated spectral weight is not explained.

concerns.quote: '...essential mechanism...' I don't understand this point. What mechanism does this suggest?
concerns.summary: The claim that the linear width narrowing implies an 'essential mechanism at zero temperature' is unclear.

concerns.quote: Can the authors please add U/W to the plots in Fig 3a?
concerns.summary: Fig. 3a should show U/W for each spectrum.

concerns.quote: Are the authors able to observe U/W <<2, and U/W >>2 that is far from the Mott criticality?
concerns.summary: The data do not show regimes far from the Mott criterion that would anchor the claim of proximity to it.

concerns.quote: Was this (fig 4b) measured on the same SoD? because as shown in fig 4d, a nm of drift can place the tip on a region with no dip.
concerns.summary: The temperature and field comparisons of the 1T gap may be confounded by tip drift between clusters.

concerns.quote: I am not sure if the authors have demonstrated that the observed zero bias dip is a superconducting gap. Can the authors please show a vortex map on the 1T surface?
concerns.summary: The 1T zero-bias dip is called superconducting without a vortex map or detailed temperature and field evolution with fits.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The zero-bias feature in Fig. 4e resembles a Fano resonance, which can appear as a peak, dip, or asymmetric line shape depending on tip-sample tunneling conditions.
concerns.summary: The dip (and the peak-dip shape where the flat-band peak nears 0 mV) could be a Fano or Kondo-related line shape, or a dip arising near Mott criticality, rather than a superconducting gap.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Its suppression with field and temperature could also arise from proximity to the 1H layer whose ability to screen correlations in 1T layer changes across its Tc.
concerns.summary: Field and temperature suppression of the dip could reflect a change in 1H screening across its Tc rather than 1T superconductivity.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The authors claim SC gap vanishes with increasing electron doping. however, I see in fig 4d that the SC gap (or a zero-bias dip) exists even when the 'peak of the flat band' is at 4-7.5 mV.
concerns.summary: Fig. 4d appears inconsistent with the Fig. 4e claim that the gap vanishes with filling; it is unclear whether both come from the same dataset, and the wide-energy spectra are missing.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Why does SFig 10a not show any splitting as compared to SFig 10c? How does the position of the LHB effect the splitting?
concerns.summary: The Zeeman splitting of the central peak appears in some clusters but not others without explanation.

concerns.quote: Fig 1c inset: please add a scale bar.
concerns.summary: Fig. 1c inset lacks a scale bar.

concerns.quote: why are the authors comparing with the band structure of monolayer 1T tas2? ... I would prefer a 4hb slab DFT calculation and showing the projected bands and dos on the 1t termination.
concerns.summary: The DFT comparison uses isolated monolayer 1T-TaS2 rather than a 4Hb slab with projected 1T bands and DOS.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Fig 3a: does this range from 0.2e to 1e, the same as Fig 2d?
concerns.summary: The filling range of Fig. 3a is not stated.

concerns.quote: I am not sure which features are being referred to as the LHB and UHB for low electron filling plots in Fig 3a and Fig 2d. Can the authors please explicitly label it
concerns.summary: Which features are the Hubbard bands at low filling is not identified.

concerns.quote: Please show the representative plots (not just fig 3b where it's clear to identify the three peaks) for all of these analysis in the supplementary.
concerns.summary: Only the clearest three-peak fit is shown; representative fits across filling are needed to judge the Fig. 3c-f parameters.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Fig 4: Please specify the STM setup conditions.
concerns.summary: Fig. 4 lacks STM setup conditions.

concerns.quote: Can the authors please label/indicate the 'peak of the flat band' in Fig 4b and d ... I am not sure I fully understand what this 'peak' feature is.
concerns.summary: The 'peak of the flat band' used to sort Fig. 4e is undefined and unmarked in Figs. 4b and 4d.

later_concerns.quote: The authors provide detailed quantitative analysis of their data and Anderson impurity model, but only hand-wave when it comes to Brinkman-Rice explanation. This is unacceptable
later_concerns.summary: Round-1 reply to C1 was qualitative; R1 demands the expected Brinkman-Rice peak width, its doping and temperature evolution, and line shape.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: Assuming Kondo temperature as a free parameter, the authors reach an excellent fit of their data which suggests that the observed peak might simply be a Kondo peak
later_concerns.summary: The new free-T_K fit works well, so the peak may be Kondo with a mis-extracted T_K.

later_concerns.quote: it is not always the case that a p-d model becomes insulating when correlations are strong. ... a 1+13 PAM is used as well.
later_concerns.summary: The authors' argument against a periodic Anderson model is flawed; the cited prior work itself uses one.

later_concerns.quote: I was interested in understanding why the authors decided to employ both. Is NRG used as a benchmark for QMC + analytic continuation?
later_concerns.summary: Why both DMFT solvers were used is still not explained.

later_concerns.quote: The upper cut off for the narrow band seems to be marked by negative dI/dV. If that is the case, then I don't think it is appropriate to interpret dI/dV as density of states
later_concerns.summary: The filling estimate's integration cutoffs are arbitrary and negative dI/dV undermines reading dI/dV as DOS.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: Fig R3-4. Perhaps the scale should be in nm instead of cm.
later_concerns.summary: Wrong unit on a rebuttal vortex-map scale bar.

later_concerns.quote: I would recommend the authors to stress these two points in their text - that this procedure has been established and explicitly state that they rule out the Kondo explanation based on this very procedure.
later_concerns.summary: R1 accepts, asking the text to state that the Kondo exclusion rests on an established parameter-extraction procedure.

later_concerns.quote: this is a consequence of accepting charge transfer as the underlying explanation for the physics. What if, for example, delocalized carriers are needed _within_ the layer to screen the correlated sites/impurities?
later_concerns.summary: The Hubbard-plus-reservoir model presupposes the charge-transfer picture it is meant to support.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

first_round.quote: It is an interesting research, but I would like my question below to be answered well before I can make a recommendation.
are therefore in principle suitable publication in Nature Communications... Once the authors have addressed these points, I will be happy to recommend publication.

the claim of observing superconductivity on the 1T surface—and its purported competition with local “paramagnetic puddles”—is not fully convincing. Additional clarification and justification are needed to support these conclusions.

recommendations.note: All recommendations come from Version 0, and none of the three referees used a standard recommendation term, so all are inferred. R1 withheld a recommendation pending answers to nine substantive questions, including a quantitative comparison of the Kondo and Brinkman-Rice scenarios; this is read as major revision. R2 judged the work in principle suitable and asked mainly for justification of the theoretical model and more detail on methods; this is read as minor revision. R3 asked for substantial new data and analysis (vortex maps, temperature and field evolution of the gap with fits, 4Hb slab DFT) to support a key claim; this is read as major revision. The file shows no sign of a transfer from another journal, and no referee co-signed another's report.
recommendations.label: contested
